arxiv_id.description: e.g. 2408.11743; null when no arXiv version exists

venue.description: sigcomm and cais added 2026-10-05 (schema authority pass). Before them the only honest encoding for a SIGCOMM or ACM CAIS paper was venue='other' with the real venue in free-text notes, which is exactly what three wave-4 records had to do. Both values were verified against the PUBLISHER'S OWN Crossref deposit before being added, never against an arXiv comment string: SIGCOMM 2025 via DOI 10.1145/3718958.3750506 (container-title 'Proceedings of the ACM SIGCOMM 2025 Conference', event "SIGCOMM '25: ACM SIGCOMM 2025 Conference", pages 592-608, issued 2025-08-27, published-print 2025-09-08) and ACM CAIS '26 via DOI 10.1145/3786335.3813124 (container-title 'Proceedings of the ACM Conference on AI and Agentic Systems', event "CAIS '26", pages 1009-1022, issued 2026-05-26). sigcomm is a CONFERENCE and is NOT interchangeable with the existing 'sigmod' member, which is a different ACM Special Interest Group. THREE records were reclassified from 'other' in the same commit: w4p-megascale-infer-disaggregated-expert-parallelism (SIGCOMM '25), w4p-xgrammar2-dynamic-agentic-structured-generation (CAIS '26) and paper-cachegen (SIGCOMM '24, DOI 10.1145/3651890.3672274).

venue_track.description: which track within the venue. Added because ACL-family Findings and EACL were UNDER-CLAIMED: a Findings paper has no honest value in `venue`, and `other` cannot separate 'published at a second-tier venue' from 'venue not yet known'. Additive only — `venue` is untouched so no existing paper record can break. findings = the companion proceedings volume; workshop = a workshop paper; industry = industry track (SysML, ICPE); unknown = track not established.

problem.description: the bottleneck it attacks, in one sentence

mechanism.description: how it works, concretely enough to implement

hardware_relevance.description: bare accelerator ids where the method's benefit is hardware-dependent

speedup_reported.description: the paper's own claim, with baseline and settings; never a bare number

sources.description: source ids; each must exist in data/sources/

venue_kind.description: Distinguishes whether the venue is a conference or journal. Added to distinguish journal venues (tmlr, taslp, jmlr, acm-tos, nature) from conference venues.

x-notes-other-venue-survey-2026-10-05.why: `other` is NOT a single state. After the sigcomm/cais pass it still holds 18 papers spanning at least nine DISTINCT venues, which is the whole problem: a reader filtering venue=other cannot tell 'published somewhere I could not name' from 'venue not yet known'. This survey is recorded here so the next schema pass does not re-derive it, and so no value is added on the strength of a notes sentence alone.

x-notes-other-venue-survey-2026-10-05.rule_learned: The lesson from this pass is that venue='other' was mostly a PROVENANCE problem, not a vocabulary problem. Ten of the eighteen records name a real, verifiable venue that simply had no enum member; several of those DO have publisher deposits sitting in this repo's own data/sources/ already. Adding a member without reclassifying every record that will use it is what produced 36 dead enum values in this repo before, so each addition here is deliberately paired with its records.
